panels.caption: Every layer rests on the one below it. Each was someone's life work.

panels.text: Every layer of computing's history rests on the one below it. Turing's idea made hardware meaningful. Hardware made languages possible. Languages made Unix practical. Unix shaped the Internet. The Internet fed machine learning. Machine learning became deep learning. Deep learning produced Transformers. Transformers enabled LLMs. LLMs became agents. And now, agents are becoming swarms.

panels.text: Ninety years of ideas, stacked like layers of a building. Each one was someone's life work. Each one seemed like the peak of what was possible — until the next layer appeared.

Multi-agent systems are the newest layer. Not the last. Almost certainly not the most important one that will ever be built. But they represent something profound: the moment when AI stopped being a solo performer and started being a team player.

panels.text: The frameworks are still evolving. The patterns are still being discovered. The best multi-agent architectures of 2030 probably have not been invented yet. What we have today — the Constellation Pattern, hierarchical orchestration, file-based communication, git worktrees — these are the first drafts. Powerful, practical, but early.

The question is no longer "Can AI write code?" That was answered. The question is no longer "Can AI work autonomously?" That was answered too. The new question is: "How do we organize teams of AI agents to tackle problems that no single mind — human or artificial — can hold all at once?"

A white speech bubble with black outline above. Inside the bubble the text reads: "The old question was can machines think. The new one is bigger." panels.speaker: QUESTBOT

panels.text: "90 years of computing history, and the core insight has not changed: the way to tackle problems too big for one mind is to organize many minds, each focused on its part, communicating through simple, universal interfaces. From Turing's tape to the swarm's files — the principle endures."

"You have just read the entire arc from a single imaginary machine in 1936 to teams of AI agents in 2026. What do you think the NEXT layer of the stack will be? What problem is too hard for today's swarms that will need something new?"

panels.text: In Issue 10, we zoom all the way out. The full stack. The full story. Every layer, every connection, every person who built a piece of the world you live in. And a question you were not expecting: what is YOUR place in the stack?
